scale: GO 2026-07-26, ChEBI lite 256, ore_ont_3836 and 13482 of the ORE 2015 EL sample, and the 12 small ORE 2015 DL files of roadmap item 709

manifest.build: mbx build --release -p sparkles-owl --example el_classify. The lane binary lane1 was built on stanley from the tree of f93ad3cb before its Cargo.toml comment was final. The others were built on atlas by atlas/build.sh.txt, with the codegen units of sparkles-owl appended to Cargo.toml for the cgu sides. lane1 and s2cgu1 come from the same code and place every function of the saturation at the same address.

sides.lane1: the lane, f93ad3cb: a worker per rule set and one codegen unit
sides.s2: the lane's worker per rule set with four codegen units
sides.s2cgu1: the lane's code with one codegen unit, built on atlas
sides.s2cgu2: the lane's code with two codegen units

method: Each part's ab.sh.txt held the bench and heavy locks and ran one el_classify process per side, file and thread count with --repeat 5, in an order of the sides that rotates each round. Each round's value is the process's median classification time. gate: Five rounds of the base and the lane, unpinned, on one and eight threads, as the earlier records of this suite ran. screen: Three rounds of the base, the two reference commits, the base with one codegen unit and the lane's code built on atlas, unpinned. pinned-t8: Six rounds on eight threads with each process pinned to the performance cores 0 to 11, which removes the placement of threads on the efficiency cores from the spread. pinned-t1-cgu2: Four rounds on one thread pinned to CPU 4, of the base, the lane and the lane's code with two codegen units.

build_time.note: buildtime.txt times mbx build --release -p sparkles-server after a new comment line in sparkles-owl, with the --timings duration of each unit. buildtime-owl.txt times mbx build --release -p sparkles-owl --lib the same way. Its third round reused the incremental state of a comment-only change and is not a build of the crate. builds.txt gives the build of the el_classify example after each new commit or setting.

perf_stat.note: User-space counters of one process on CPU 4 with --repeat 3 on one thread, the read included.

notes: Every side gives the same taxonomy of each file on one and eight threads. The unpinned gate's eight-thread rounds of ChEBI lite spread by 15% on both sides and put the lane 5.6% above the base, while the pinned eight-thread part puts it 5.9% below with the same spread, so the eight-thread difference on ChEBI lite is within the noise that roadmap item 683 follows.
